title: eng-platform
text:
eng-platform

Logan Wright: trying to close the loop on perf-canary histograms before we roll into more regions. adding 4–6 new histograms (e2e latency, runtime latency, prefill, decode, queue) *per model* is going to move our Mimir bill. can someone sanity check retention + downsampling strategy?

Nadia Rahman: yep. I pulled rough numbers from current canary series + proposed hist buckets.

Nadia Rahman: assumptions:
- 10 models (top + high-risk), 3 regions phase-2, 2 SKUs in us-east
- labels we *keep*: model, model_version, region, sku, tier, runtime_build
- 5 histograms, each w/ 12 buckets (+ _sum/_count)

Nadia Rahman: worst case series multiplier is ugly:
- 5 hists * (12 buckets + sum + count) = 5 * 14 = 70 time series per unique labelset
- today we’re ~18–25 series per labelset for canary

Nadia Rahman: if we keep runtime_build + model_version on the raw hist, we basically create a new labelset per rollout (and Mimir churns), and retention cost is mostly driven by *ingested samples*.

Caleb Johnson: +1. also worth noting: histograms sampled at 15s scrape = 4x samples vs 60s. we should not be scraping canary hists at 15s unless we really need that granularity.

Logan Wright: current plan from Omar’s PR was 30s interval for canary metrics. is 60s acceptable for alerting p95/p99?

Allison Grant: for paging: yes. our alert windows are 10–30m. 60s scrape is fine.

Allison Grant: bigger issue is we shouldn’t retain raw bucket series forever. standards doc says “high-cardinality + hist buckets must have a rollup plan”.

Omar El-Sayed: from runtime side: we *need* bucketed hist in the short term for triage (seeing tail shape). but we don’t need 6mo of tail shape. we mostly need p50/p95/p99 + count to compare to baseline.

Nadia Rahman: exactly. best practice here:
1) keep raw hist buckets short retention (7–14d)
2) compute quantiles via recording rules and retain *those* longer
3) optionally store a coarser histogram (fewer buckets) longer if we really need distribution shape

Caleb Johnson: we can do (2) w/ recording rules in the observability-pack. ex:
```
record: perf_canary:model_p95_latency_ms
expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, model, region, sku, tier) (rate(perf_canary_latency_ms_bucket[5m])))
```

Caleb Johnson: then alerts/dashboards mostly read the recording rules. raw buckets only for drill-down.

Logan Wright: if we drop model_version + runtime_build from buckets, does that kill our ability to correlate regressions to rollouts?

Allison Grant: we can keep runtime_build as an *annotation* via logs/traces + alert payload. don’t put it on every bucket series.

Nadia Rahman: +1. if we must keep something, keep a low-churn version tag like `runtime_release` (e.g. 2026.02.05) not full build SHA, and only on the *derived* quantile series, not buckets.

Omar El-Sayed: tagging:
- runtime_build_id changes multiple times/day in canary env
- runtime_release changes 1–2x/week
- kernel_id can change per request based on auto-select 😬

Omar El-Sayed: I’m strongly in favor of NOT putting kernel_id on hist metrics. we can emit kernel_id as a sampled log field and link from the dashboard to logs.

Caleb Johnson: kernel_id on hist = cardinality timebomb.

Logan Wright: ok. let’s get concrete. Nadia, can you quantify cost delta for 14d raw buckets + long-lived quantiles?

Nadia Rahman: rough back-of-napkin from Mimir stats + current sample costs:
- if we keep raw buckets 90d: +$18–24k/month at phase-2 coverage
- if raw buckets 14d + derived quantiles 13mo: +$4–6k/month
- if raw buckets 7d + derived quantiles 13mo: +$3–4k/month

Nadia Rahman: variability mainly from whether we include model_version/region/sku/tier all together.

Allison Grant: I’m fine with 14d buckets. oncall usually needs <7d, but 14d covers “regression started last Friday” cases.

Caleb Johnson: we should also downsample in-query by increasing rate window. but that doesn’t reduce storage. retention is the lever.

Logan Wright: what about “downsampling” inside Mimir (compactor)? do we have that enabled?

Nadia Rahman: not real downsampling of raw series. we have blocks + retention, but it’s still storing the samples. the practical approach is: shorter retention on raw, longer on recorded series.

GrafanaBot: Reminder: Metric retention changes require updating `metrics-retention.yaml` and notifying #eng-sre per policy.

Logan Wright: got it.

Allison Grant: also: exemplars. are we emitting exemplars on hist buckets?

Caleb Johnson: right now traces are sampled independently. if we add exemplars for every canary request we’ll pay twice (exemplar storage + trace storage). I’d keep exemplars OFF for canary metrics.

Omar El-Sayed: can do. we’ll include trace_id as a *log field* on the canary job, and dashboard can link to logs->trace.

Logan Wright: scrape interval: proposing 60s for all hist buckets + quantiles. any objections?

Allison Grant: no.

Nadia Rahman: +1. if we need faster during incident we can temporarily drop to 30s via config, but default 60s.

Logan Wright: buckets: do we really need 12 buckets? can we do 8–10?

Omar El-Sayed: for latency we care about sub-100ms vs 100–300 vs 300–1000 vs >1s. 10 buckets is fine.

Caleb Johnson: and keep bucket boundaries consistent across all latency histograms. makes dashboards + queries easier.

Nadia Rahman: please don’t do per-model bucket configs.

Logan Wright: ok.

Logan Wright: proposal (to lock):
- Raw histogram buckets retention: 14d
- Derived series via recording rules: p50/p95/p99 + count + avg (sum/count), retention 13mo
- Scrape interval: 60s for canary metrics
- Labels on raw buckets: model, region, sku, tier (NO model_version, NO runtime_build_id, NO kernel_id)
- Labels on derived quantiles: model, region, sku, tier + runtime_release (low churn)
- Exemplars: OFF

Allison Grant: looks good. please add a note in the ADR that kernel/runtime build attribution is via alert payload links + logs/traces, not metric labels.

Caleb Johnson: I’ll open a PR in observability-pack for the recording rules + switch dashboards to use the recorded series by default.

Nadia Rahman: I’ll update the retention config + add a small “expected cost impact” blurb for SRE review.

Omar El-Sayed: I’ll adjust metric label set in the canary emitter and remove build/kernel tags from the hist metrics.

Logan Wright: thanks. I’ll paste this into the rollout checklist + tag @Rafael Mendes/@Aisha Bello once the PRs are up so oncall isn’t surprised.

Allison Grant: :thumbsup:

Caleb Johnson: :thumbsup:

Nadia Rahman: :thumbsup:
